title: What are approval rules in workflow automation? How to write them
description: Approval rules are written, checkable sentences that say what software may prepare on its own and what must wait for a person to confirm.

summary.question: What are approval rules in workflow automation?
summary.answer: Approval rules are written, checkable sentences that say what software may prepare on its own and what must wait for a person to confirm. They are agreed before anything goes live, so the team stays in control of every decision that matters.
takeaways: Write each approval rule as one sentence a reviewer can check.
List the decisions that stay with people first: pricing, discounts, refunds, exceptions, and any legal or safety judgement.
Decide which messages need review before they go out. With CarSalesTeam, your team reviews external messages.
Give every request outside the rules a named handoff, and record it.
Change rules in writing at a scheduled review, not on the fly.

scope.covers: What approval rules are, which decisions they should keep with people, how to word them and how to change them once the workflow is live.
scope.excludes: Rules for a specific software product, legal or regulatory advice, and price figures.
scope.instead: Routing the requests the rules hand back to people is covered in the guide to exceptions.

sections.heading: What is an approval rule?
paragraphs: An approval rule is one sentence that says what may be prepared automatically and what must wait for a person. A good rule is specific enough that a reviewer can look at a single request and say whether the rule was followed.
For example: do not confirm a test drive without staff confirmation. That rule names the action, the person who confirms it, and what happens without them.

sections.heading: Which decisions should stay with people?
paragraphs: Start by listing what software should never decide. Everything else is written relative to that list.
list: Any legal, financial or safety judgement.

sections.heading: Which messages need review before they go out?
paragraphs: Decide in advance which outgoing messages a person must see first. With CarSalesTeam, your team reviews external messages before they go out, and CarSalesTeam does not book, change or confirm anything on its own.

sections.heading: How do you write a rule a reviewer can check?
list: Name the action, for example confirming a test drive or a service appointment.
Name who approves it, for example the sales manager or the service desk.
Say what happens when approval is missing: the request waits, or it is handed to a named person.
Avoid words like appropriate or reasonable that two reviewers could read differently.

sections.heading: What happens to a request outside the rules?
paragraphs: Every rule set needs a handoff path. Agree who receives a request the rules do not cover, and how the handoff is recorded, so it is counted as an exception rather than lost.

sections.heading: How do approval rules change once the workflow is live?
paragraphs: Review results, exceptions and staff time on a regular schedule. When a rule needs to change, change it in writing at that review, so everyone knows which rules are in force.

sections.heading: What do example rules look like at a dealership?
paragraphs: These examples are illustrative and follow the limits stated on the CarSalesTeam home page.
list: Sales: verify vehicle availability and appointment capacity before confirming a test drive.
Service: use approved service categories and scheduling access, and do not diagnose a fault.
Commercial: discounts, trade-in valuations and financing commitments require authorised staff.

faq.q: What are approval rules in workflow automation?
faq.a: Approval rules are written, checkable sentences that say what software may prepare on its own and what must wait for a person to confirm. They are agreed before anything goes live.

faq.q: Who should write the approval rules?
faq.a: The team that owns the workflow, with the person who reviews the results. They know which decisions carry risk.

faq.q: Does CarSalesTeam send messages to customers on its own?
faq.a: No. Your team reviews external messages before they go out, and approval rules are agreed before anything goes live.

faq.q: Can approval rules change once the workflow is live?
faq.a: Yes, in writing at a scheduled review. Any change to the scope itself is agreed separately first.
